title: 6 Best Grout Sealers in 2026: Shower, Floor and Stone Picks
metaDescription: A grout sealer coat lasts about 1 to 3 years: Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold is the best for most homes and StoneTech BulletProof the top shower pick.

intro:
The best grout sealer for most homes is Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold, a water-based penetrating sealer rated for cement grout and porous tile or stone, indoors and out. For a shower, StoneTech BulletProof is the top pick because it is approved for wet areas and has a mild odor in a closed bathroom.

Grout is the sponge in a tiled room. Cement grout soaks up coffee, mop water, body oils and soap, which is why light joints turn gray long before the tile wears. A penetrating sealer slows that down so dirt rinses away. It does not make grout waterproof, it does not prevent mold by itself, and it does nothing on epoxy grout.
quickAnswer: Buy Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold for most floors, counters and backsplashes, and StoneTech BulletProof for showers. Use Miracle Sealants 511 Impregnator on natural stone tile, Black Diamond Ultimate Grout Sealer for large ceramic floors on a budget, and Tuff Duck spray for quick backsplash jobs. If the grout is already stained, Polyblend Grout Renew recolors and seals it.

sections.heading: The 6 Best Grout Sealers in 2026, Ranked
sections.body:
Rankings are based on manufacturer data sheets, the surfaces and wet areas each label approves, stated cure and reapply times, and recurring owner feedback on staining and ease of use. Penetrating sealers rank ahead of coatings because they suit the widest range of grout and tile.

### Best Overall: Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold

Sealer's Choice Gold is the flagship water-based impregnator from Aqua Mix, a brand many tile setters keep in the truck. Its label covers cement grout plus natural stone, unglazed porcelain and quarry tile, inside and outside, so one bottle can treat an entire bathroom or kitchen, including the tile itself when that tile is porous. It soaks in without changing the color or sheen of the joints, and the maker positions it against both water and oil, which matters on kitchen floors where grease ends up in the grout lines. Apply it to clean, dry grout, let it dwell for the time on the label, then wipe excess off the tile face before it dries. The water base keeps the smell manageable in a small room. It costs more per bottle than budget sealers, and it needs a full cure before showers or mopping.

**Pros:** Seals grout and porous tile or stone in one product; mild odor; rated for showers, floors, counters and exteriors; no visible film or gloss.

**Cons:** Premium price; needs a full cure before water exposure.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Aqua+Mix+Sealer%27s+Choice+Gold&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Showers: StoneTech BulletProof Stone and Grout Sealer

Showers are the hardest place for grout. Hot water, soap, shampoo and body oils hit the joints every day, and grout that absorbs them stays damp longer and darkens faster. StoneTech BulletProof is a water-based penetrating sealer approved for grout, natural stone and porous tile, including shower wet zones. It cuts absorption without forming a slick film that could cloud or peel, and its mild odor is a real advantage in a bathroom without a window. The catch is timing: the grout must be fully dry, which in a shower usually means a couple of days out of use beforehand, and then the shower stays dry for the cure time on the label afterward. On new or very porous grout, plan for two coats. It is priced above budget grout sealers, which is reasonable for a surface that sees water twice a day.

**Pros:** Approved for showers and wet areas; low odor; works on grout and natural stone; no change in appearance once cured.

**Cons:** Costs more than budget options; often needs two coats on new grout.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=StoneTech+BulletProof+Stone+and+Grout+Sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Stone Tile: Miracle Sealants 511 Impregnator

511 Impregnator has been on tile-shop shelves for decades, and it earns its place on stone floors. Because it is labeled for natural stone as well as grout, a travertine or marble floor with cement grout gets even protection in one pass instead of a joint-by-joint job. The thin solvent carrier reaches into tight, older grout that some water-based products struggle to enter. The trade-off is smell. In a windowless bathroom, run the fan, prop the door open and, ideally, do it when the household can be elsewhere for a few hours. Wipe excess off polished stone promptly, because dried residue shows up as haze in raking light. On glazed ceramic with cement grout, a water-based sealer and an applicator bottle are usually easier. For counters and slabs, see the [granite sealer](/best-granite-sealer/) and [marble sealer](/best-marble-sealer/) picks.

**Pros:** Solvent carrier gets deep into dense grout; safe for marble, travertine and limestone; long track record; no added sheen.

**Cons:** Strong odor; residue on polished stone must be wiped quickly.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Miracle+Sealants+511+Impregnator&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Budget: Black Diamond Stoneworks Ultimate Grout Sealer

Black Diamond aims its Ultimate Grout Sealer at homeowners with a lot of floor to cover. It is water based, goes on easily with a brush, sponge or roller, and is sold in sizes up to a gallon, which suits open kitchens, mudrooms and basements tiled in ceramic or porcelain. Protection against water and everyday dirt is solid. Where it gives ground to premium products is oil resistance and longevity: in kitchens where grease lands in the joints, or in showers with heavy product use, Aqua Mix or BulletProof will hold out longer. On a big ceramic floor, though, the math favors it. Sealing every joint with a premium product adds up fast, and resealing every year or two with an affordable one is an easy afternoon. The mild odor makes that routine painless.

**Pros:** Low cost per square foot; easy water-based application; gallon sizes for big floors; mild odor.

**Cons:** Lighter oil protection than premium sealers; more frequent resealing in busy areas.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Black+Diamond+Stoneworks+Ultimate+Grout+Sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Value Spray: Tuff Duck Granite, Grout and Marble Sealer

Tuff Duck comes in a trigger spray bottle, and that format is the whole appeal. There is nothing to pour or measure, so a kitchen backsplash or small bathroom floor becomes a weeknight job. The water-based formula is labeled for grout as well as granite and marble. Spray along the joints, let it soak in, then wipe overspray from the tile before it dries. On glazed ceramic it wipes off easily; on polished stone, wipe promptly to avoid streaks. Its protection level suits backsplashes and low-traffic floors well. For a shower used twice a day or a busy kitchen floor, a dedicated impregnator is worth the extra cost. The bottle is also small for large floors, so buy a different product for anything over a modest bathroom.

**Pros:** Ready-to-use spray; low odor; works on grout and natural stone; inexpensive for small jobs.

**Cons:** Overspray must be wiped off tile; small bottle for large floors.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Tuff+Duck+Granite+Grout+and+Marble+Sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Stained Grout: Custom Building Products Polyblend Grout Renew

Grout Renew is not a clear sealer. It is a colorant that coats each joint with a pigmented, sealing layer, which hides stains no cleaner can lift and lets you change the grout color without chiseling anything out. That makes it the fix for older floors where light gray grout has turned patchy brown. Prep matters more than with any clear sealer: the grout must be clean, dry and free of soap film or old sealer so the colorant bonds. Apply it with a small brush along each joint, wipe the tile edges with a damp cloth, then remove any film from the tile face as the label directs. It is slow work on a large floor. Pick a color that matches or is slightly darker than the original, since going lighter takes more coats and shows misses.

**Pros:** Recolors and seals in one step; hides permanent stains; many standard grout colors; avoids regrouting.

**Cons:** Slow, joint-by-joint application; it is a coating, so prep is critical.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Polyblend+Grout+Renew&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.heading: What Is the Best Grout Sealer for a Shower?
sections.body:
StoneTech BulletProof is the best grout sealer for most showers, with Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold a close second. Both are penetrating, approved for wet areas and low in odor, which is what a shower needs.

### Why penetrating beats membrane in a shower

Topical or membrane sealers form a film on the grout. In a shower, water and vapor get behind that film, it clouds over and then peels. A penetrating sealer stays inside the grout and lets it dry out between showers, so there is nothing to fail.

### Shower floors versus walls

Shower floors sit in standing water and take the most wear, so they lose protection first. Seal the floor and the lowest two or three rows of wall tile with extra care, and check them every few months with a few drops of water.

### Timing a shower job

Keep the shower out of use for 24 to 48 hours before sealing so the joints dry out. After sealing, keep it dry for the cure time on the label, commonly 24 to 72 hours. A guest bathroom or a weekend away makes that easier.

### Habits that matter more than the sealer

Squeegee the walls after use and run the exhaust fan for 20 to 30 minutes. Grout that dries quickly grows far less mildew, sealed or not. If mildew is already there, clean it first; our [mold remover guide](/best-mold-remover/) covers products that work on grout and caulk.

sections.heading: Do You Need to Seal Grout?
sections.body:
For cement-based grout, yes in most kitchens, bathrooms and entries. For epoxy and most premixed urethane grouts, no.

### Cement grout

Sanded and unsanded cement grouts are the most common in homes. Once cured they are porous, so water, oil and dirt travel into them. This is the grout that benefits from sealing, and nearly every product above is made for it.

### Epoxy grout

Epoxy grout is a two-part resin that cures dense and nonporous. It resists stains on its own and does not absorb sealer. A penetrating sealer applied to it just dries on top as a sticky or hazy film.

### Urethane and premixed grouts

Many single-component premixed grouts are sold as never needing sealer because their resin binder already resists stains. If the maker says no sealer is needed, believe it.

### How to tell which you have

Check the installer's paperwork, a leftover grout bag or the builder's finish schedule. If none exists, drop a little water on a joint. Unsealed cement grout darkens within a minute or two. Epoxy will not change at all and looks slightly glossy. A joint that beads water for ten minutes is either epoxy or cement grout with a working seal.

sections.heading: Penetrating, Membrane or Colorant: Which Type of Grout Sealer?
sections.body:
Penetrating sealers are the right type for most grout. The other two have narrow jobs.

| Type | How it works | Changes look? | Best use | Avoid on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Penetrating impregnator | Soaks into pores | No | Showers, floors, backsplashes | Epoxy grout |
| Membrane or topical | Forms a surface film | Adds sheen | Low-moisture decorative walls | Showers, floors |
| Colorant | Pigmented coating | Yes, recolors | Stained or mismatched grout | Wet, dirty or sealed grout |
| None needed | Already dense | No | Epoxy and many urethane grouts | Not applicable |

### Penetrating sealers

They line the pores with water- and oil-repellent compounds, keep the grout breathable and never peel. The chemistry varies by brand: some use fluoropolymers, others silane or siloxane. Our [silane vs siloxane](/silane-vs-siloxane-sealers/) guide explains how those repellents behave on masonry.

### Membrane sealers

They repel water strongly at first and may add sheen, but in wet areas they trap moisture, cloud and peel, and on floors they wear unevenly along traffic paths.

### Colorants

They are a restoration product, not routine maintenance. Because they bond as a coating, they need clean, dry, unsealed grout.

sections.heading: Miracle 511 vs Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold vs StoneTech BulletProof: Which Is Best?
sections.body:
For most homes, Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold. For a shower, StoneTech BulletProof. For natural stone tile where you want tile and grout treated together and do not mind solvent odor, Miracle 511 Impregnator.

| Factor | Sealer's Choice Gold | BulletProof | 511 Impregnator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Carrier | Water | Water | Solvent |
| Odor | Mild | Mild | Strong |
| Shower approved | Yes, per label | Yes, per label | Check label for wet use |
| Natural stone | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Best fit | Whole rooms, kitchens | Showers, bathrooms | Stone floors |

### What separates them

All three are penetrating and leave no sheen. The real differences are the carrier and the job they suit. Water carriers make the two water-based sealers easy to live with in an occupied home. The solvent in 511 helps it get into dense, older grout, at the cost of fumes.

### Looking for an alternative to another premium sealer?

If your usual premium impregnator is out of stock, Sealer's Choice Gold is the most widely available substitute with a similar job description: water based, rated for grout and porous stone, indoor and outdoor. Read both labels before switching mid-project, and do not layer different brands on the same joints without testing a small area first.

sections.heading: What Is the Best Grout Sealer for Exterior Stone and Patio Tile?
sections.body:
Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold is the best choice here among the picks, because its label covers exterior use on grout and porous stone. Outdoor grout faces rain, freeze-thaw and sun, so it needs a breathable penetrating sealer rather than a film.

### Why films fail outside

A topical sealer on an outdoor patio traps moisture from the slab below. In freezing weather that water expands behind the film, and in summer the sun breaks it down. The result is white clouding and peeling within a season or two.

### Prep for outdoor tile

Clean with a neutral tile cleaner and a stiff brush, then let the patio dry for at least a full day of dry weather, longer in shade. Seal in mild weather, roughly 50 to 90 degrees Fahrenheit, with no rain forecast for a day.

### Pavers are a different job

If your patio is pavers set on sand rather than tile set in grout, the joint material is sand or polymeric sand and the right product is a paver sealer. See our [paver sealer](/best-paver-sealer/) picks. For concrete patio slabs, the [best concrete sealer](/best-concrete-sealer/) guide matches products to each kind of slab.

sections.heading: How Do You Apply Grout Sealer?
sections.body:
Wait for the grout to cure, clean it, let it dry, then apply sealer to the joints only on glazed tile, or to the whole surface on porous tile.

### Wait after grouting

Most grout makers call for at least 48 to 72 hours before sealing, longer for wide joints, cool rooms or high humidity. Check the bag. Waiting a week when in doubt costs nothing. Remove any grout haze on the tile first, because sealing over haze locks it in.

### Clean and dry existing grout

Use a pH-neutral or mildly alkaline tile cleaner and a stiff nylon brush. Rinse well so no residue remains. Avoid acid cleaners on cement grout and on marble, limestone or travertine. Then let the grout dry, 24 hours in a dry room and longer in a humid bathroom with a fan running.

### Apply neatly

On glazed ceramic or porcelain, use an applicator bottle with a small roller wheel or brush tip and run it along each joint. Wipe any sealer off the tile within a few minutes. On porous stone, terra-cotta or quarry tile, coat tile and grout together with a pad or sponge, let it dwell, then wipe off the excess.

### Second coat and cure

Most labels suggest a second coat on new or porous grout, applied once the first has soaked in, often 5 to 30 minutes later. If a water drop still darkens the grout after the first coat dries, it needs another. Work from the far corner toward the door, and keep traffic and water off for the times the label lists.

### Ventilation and safety

Water-based sealers are easy to use in an occupied home. Solvent products need open windows, a running fan and no pilot lights or flames nearby. Wear nitrile gloves, and spread solvent-soaked rags flat outside to dry before disposal.

sections.heading: How Long Does Grout Sealer Last, and How Much Do You Need?
sections.body:
A coat of grout sealer typically lasts 1 to 3 years: about 1 to 2 years in a shower, 1 to 3 on floors, and longer on backsplashes.

### What wears it out

Cleaning products more than anything. Bleach sprays, strong degreasers and acidic bathroom cleaners strip sealer quickly. A neutral tile and stone cleaner preserves it far longer. If you need bleach for mildew, plan to reseal sooner.

### The water drop test

Put a few drops on grout in the busiest spots. Joints that darken almost at once have lost protection; joints where water beads or sits for several minutes are still sealed. Resealing is quick: clean, dry, one coat. There is no need to strip a penetrating sealer first.

### How much to buy

Coverage is quoted per square foot of tiled area, and it swings widely with joint width and tile size. Small mosaics can have 20 percent or more of the surface in grout, while 24-inch porcelain has very little. A quart might cover around 100 square feet of mosaic or several hundred square feet of large-format tile. For a typical 5-by-8-foot bathroom floor plus a shower surround, one quart of penetrating sealer is usually enough for two coats.

### Doing it yourself or hiring out

Sealing a bathroom is an afternoon's work. Professional grout cleaning and sealing is commonly quoted per square foot, and more with colorant. The expensive outcome is regrouting a floor that was left to deteriorate, which is what routine sealing avoids.

sections.heading: How Do You Fix Grout That Is Already Stained?
sections.body:
Deep-clean first, recolor second, and regrout only as a last resort.

### Deep clean

Many grout lines that look permanently brown are just coated with soap film and mop residue. An oxygen bleach solution made from sodium percarbonate powder and warm water, left for 10 to 15 minutes and scrubbed with a stiff nylon brush, lifts a surprising amount without harming cement grout or most tile. A steam cleaner with a small brush tip is a chemical-free alternative on floors. Rinse with clean water afterward.

### Recolor

If the grout is clean but still blotchy, a colorant such as Polyblend Grout Renew gives every joint one uniform shade. Then add a clear sealer unless the colorant label says it already seals.

### Regrout

Save regrouting for grout that is cracked, crumbling or missing. Removing it with a carbide grout saw or oscillating tool is slow and dusty and can chip tile edges. Regrout only the failed sections, let them cure, then seal or color the whole area so it matches.

### Where caulk belongs instead

Grout is rigid and cracks where two planes meet: inside shower corners, along the tub, and where tile meets a countertop. Those joints move and need a flexible sealant such as 100 percent silicone. Seal the grout first, let it cure, then caulk. Our [exterior caulk](/best-exterior-caulk/) guide explains how silicone and hybrid sealants differ, and [how long caulk takes to dry](/how-long-does-caulk-take-to-dry/) covers the wait before the shower goes back into use.

mistakes.title: Sealing grout before it has cured
mistakes.body: Fresh grout still holds water. Sealing too soon traps that moisture, keeps the sealer from soaking in and can leave cloudy, blotchy joints. Follow the grout maker's wait time, usually 48 to 72 hours, and give showers, basements and humid rooms extra time.

mistakes.title: Sealing epoxy grout
mistakes.body: Epoxy grout is already nonporous, so a penetrating sealer has nowhere to go. It sits on the surface and dries into a sticky or hazy film you then have to scrub off. Confirm your grout type with the installer or a water test before buying any sealer.

mistakes.title: Letting sealer dry on glazed tile
mistakes.body: Sealer that dries on glazed ceramic or polished stone leaves streaks and haze that are hard to remove. Use an applicator bottle to keep product in the joints, and wipe drips and overspray off the tile within a few minutes, before they tack up.

mistakes.title: Sealing over dirt or mildew
mistakes.body: Sealer preserves whatever is in the grout, including soap scum, mildew and the gray film from years of mopping. Deep-clean the joints, rinse well and let them dry completely first, or the discoloration becomes permanent and the sealer bonds poorly.

mistakes.title: Cleaning sealed grout with bleach or acid
mistakes.body: Bleach sprays, acidic shower cleaners and harsh degreasers break sealer down quickly and can erode cement grout over time. Use a pH-neutral tile cleaner for routine cleaning, and save stronger products for occasional deep cleans followed by a fresh coat.

faqs.q: What is the best grout sealer?
faqs.a: Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold is the best grout sealer for most homes. It is a water-based penetrating sealer rated for cement grout and porous tile or stone, indoors and outdoors, and it leaves no sheen. For showers, StoneTech BulletProof is the stronger pick, and for natural stone floors, Miracle Sealants 511 Impregnator treats tile and grout together.

faqs.q: What is the highest rated shower grout sealer?
faqs.a: StoneTech BulletProof is the top shower grout sealer among these picks. It is a water-based penetrating sealer approved for wet areas, it has a mild odor in a closed bathroom, and it leaves no film that could cloud or peel. Keep the shower dry before and after sealing for the times on the label, and plan two coats on new grout.

faqs.q: Do I really need to seal grout?
faqs.a: For cement-based grout in kitchens, bathrooms and entries, yes in most cases. It is porous and absorbs dirt, oils and water, so it darkens over time. Sealing slows that and makes cleaning easier. Epoxy and most urethane grouts do not need sealing, so check what was installed before buying anything.

faqs.q: How long does grout sealer last?
faqs.a: Usually 1 to 3 years, depending on the product, the room and how you clean. Showers and kitchen floors wear sealer fastest, and harsh cleaners shorten its life a lot. Put a few drops of water on the joints once or twice a year; if they soak in and darken quickly, apply a fresh coat.

faqs.q: What is the best penetrating grout sealer?
faqs.a: Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold is the best all-round penetrating grout sealer, with StoneTech BulletProof best for showers and Miracle 511 Impregnator best on natural stone tile. All three soak into the grout, leave no film and keep the joints breathable, so they do not cloud or peel the way membrane sealers can.

Not by itself. Sealer reduces how much water grout absorbs, so it dries faster and mold is less likely, but mold feeds on soap residue and surface moisture. Ventilation, squeegeeing shower walls and regular cleaning matter more. A sealed, clean and well-ventilated shower is far less prone to mildew than one relying on sealer alone.

faqs.q: Is spray or brush-on grout sealer easier?
faqs.a: Brush-on and roller-tip applicators are easier on most floors because they put sealer into the joints with less waste and less wiping. Sprays such as Tuff Duck are quicker on small backsplashes but drift onto the tile, which then needs wiping. On porous stone tile, a pad or sponge over the whole surface is easiest.

bottomLine: Aqua Mix Sealer's Choice Gold is the most versatile grout sealer for most homes, and StoneTech BulletProof is the one to buy for a shower. Use Miracle 511 on natural stone tile, Black Diamond on big ceramic floors where cost matters, Tuff Duck for quick backsplash jobs, and Polyblend Grout Renew when grout is stained past saving. Whatever you choose, confirm the grout is cement based, clean it, let it dry, keep sealer off glazed tile, and do a water drop test once a year.
